title: Phase 3 — split the credential file
description: ~/.ticksrc started as a board-sync token file and now carries THIRTY KeyFactory* constants — factory_url, factory_token, factory_github_token/refresh_token/token_expires_at, factory_gateway_url/provider/key, factory_cloudflare_api_token, factory_workers_ai_billing_mode and more. Live GitHub OAuth refresh tokens and a Cloudflare API token. Either the factory writes its own file, or ticks exposes a namespaced read/write API and stops defining factory keys. Decide before anything moves. This is the ONLY step that can break a live deployment on a real machine, so it needs a migration path, not a cut.
notes:
2026-08-31 13:22 - MAPPED BEFORE PLANNING (2026-08-31). Three facts that shape this phase, none of them in the epic's original description.

1. THE FILE IS 88% FACTORY BY KEY COUNT. internal/ticksrc defines FIFTEEN KeyFactory* constants — URL, Token, Version, CloudflareAPIToken, GatewayURL/Provider/Key, GitHubAuth/Login/Repo/Token/TokenExpires/RefreshToken/RefreshExpires, WorkersAIBillingMode — against exactly TWO non-factory ones, KeyToken and KeyURL. This is not a shared file with some factory keys in it. It is a factory credentials file with two board-sync keys still living in it.

2. THERE ARE TWO INDEPENDENT READERS OF THE SAME FILE, and only one of them uses the package. internal/tickboard/cloud/client.go declares its OWN ConfigFileName = ".ticksrc" and its OWN readConfigFile() that parses the file by hand into a two-field struct. It never imports internal/ticksrc. So ~/.ticksrc is parsed twice, by two implementations, in one binary — the exact duplication class this project has been removing everywhere else, and it has no contract holding the two parsers together.

3. TWO CORE COMMANDS READ FACTORY KEYS. cmd/tk/cmd/upgrade.go:69-80 reads KeyFactoryURL and KeyFactoryVersion to warn that a deployed factory is behind. cmd/tk/cmd/board.go reads the file for board sync. upgrade is the surviving ticks->factory coupling that this phase has to answer for; board is the reader that must keep working through whatever split happens.

WHY THIS PHASE IS THE ONE THAT CAN BREAK SOMEONE: those fifteen keys include live GitHub OAuth refresh tokens and a Cloudflare API token on real machines. A cut migrates nothing; a rename strands a deployment. It needs a migration path and evidence that a populated pre-split file still authenticates afterwards.

AND THE REASON IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: Phase 4b found that tk ask/answer silently read this file and called a deployed Worker. That escape hatch existed BECAUSE factory credentials live somewhere the terminal path could reach. Splitting them is what makes that class of bug impossible rather than merely removed.
acceptance_criteria: internal/ticksrc defines no KeyFactory* constant. A machine with an existing deployed factory still authenticates after upgrading both sides, proven by a migration test over a fixture of the current file shape. The chosen split is documented in the spec.
